question_en:
I am organizing an old tour route map left by a curator. The numbers inside the colored boxes are accession numbers, and each leader line connects a gallery to the accession number of the next artwork. Please start querying the museum's single-item page from the accession number next to `START`. Based on the gallery recorded on the page, return to the map to read the next accession number. Repeat this process until you reach the gallery where `END` is located. Please answer the following questions:

1. Which artwork corresponds to `START`? What are its formal title and artist?
2. Excluding the start and end points, which galleries are passed through in order? Please list the gallery name, formal title of the artwork, and the carpet style name recorded in the museum's data for each stop in walking order.
3. Which artwork corresponds to `END`? Please provide its formal title, artist attribution, and accession number.

Answer Format: Please answer in points numbered (1)–(3); answer questions 1 and 3 in text; for question 2, use a table to list the gallery name, formal title of the artwork, and carpet style name in walking order.
answer:
(1) Formal title: David Sinton; Artist: Hiram Powers.

(2)

| Order | Gallery Name | Formal Title of Artwork | Carpet Style Name |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Green Parlor (8) | Teapot with Flowers, Birds, and Bamboo | Empire Medallion |
| 2 | Music Room (14) | Charles Phelps Taft | Peony |
| 3 | Dining Room (12) | Village Interior | Kykuit (Codman) Turkey |
| 4 | Virtue & Vice (6) | Teapot with Two Boys Among Peony Blossoms | Parquet with Ebony |

(3) Formal title: Plaque with Cupid and a Goose; Artist attribution: Attributed to Giovanni Bernardi; Accession number: 1931.207.
